video.genre: AI explainer and opinion, partly screen-shared

protocol.status: v2 labeler B (rubric v2), independent of A
protocol.note: Drafted from the transcript alone, without seeing any jevcut output or other labels.
protocol.times_from: Lemonfox transcript; seconds in the source, so labels survive re-transcription

clips.why: Claim: the cost of the model is not the cost of the harness around it. Chat is a thin harness; coding agents are a thick one; payoff 107.1: per Anthropic, agents or multi-agent systems cost 4-15x more.

Worked example: a 25-token prompt costs about a cent via the model, but 37 cents in Claude Code, ~30x; the harness adds 8k-30k tokens to every message, 'a toll gate' (163.2), and that overhead is the system prompt (166.1). Screen-shared, but every number is spoken.

Surprising back-of-envelope: an H100 rents for ~$3/hr, can hold a 1M-token context, and 12 five-minute cache slots make ~$70/hr in caching revenue, 'which is huge' (404.3). 357.1 opens on Anthropic's one-hour cache pricing for context; 415.2 adds the quantization caveat.

also_ok.why: A prompt isn't sent once: the harness and model loop (check file, create file, write contents); long tasks mean many round trips, each carrying the system-prompt toll gate (313.0). A clear explanation but the step-by-step example makes it run over band.
Vendors keep people in a walled garden by selling a subscription that covers the harness, so you don't panic mid-task over what the agent spends. Short; leads into the sponsor.

negatives.why: Open models catching up by 6-18 months, list of models, 'taking up so much space in the leaderboard, as you can see'.
Per-harness price comparison (37c/11c/7c/2.5c): numbers read off the screen, 'the same prompt from earlier'.
Speculation on one-hour cache writes spilling to SSD; opens on 'the pricing model changes a bit' and depends on the preceding math.
Sponsor read (Cline Pass), posed as a question about vendor lock-in.
